I visited Madhu Agarwal Maternity & Nursing Home (Bhayander West) after seeing their high rating and number of positive reviews — but unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing.

After visiting, I realized that most of those 5-star reviews are not genuine. The doctors themselves take patients’ phones and post positive reviews, which is highly unethical. Both Dr. Madhu Agarwal and Dr. Nikita Agarwal seem to be completely money-minded, with little concern for patient care.

Dr. Nikita Agarwal in particular is extremely rude — not just to patients, but even to their family members. Several genuine reviews also mention the same, and I can now confirm it’s true.

Surprisingly, being a maternity hospital, they appear to have little patience or affection for babies. They don’t allow small children in the consultation room and even scold parents for holding their baby’s hand.

On top of that, their charges are exorbitant:

UPT kit costing ₹100 elsewhere is billed at ₹500, CBC ₹500, Ultrasonography ₹3000+ (recommended multiple times unnecessarily)

Medicines sold at inflated rates — items worth ₹60 charged in thousands.

These rates are far higher than what other maternity centers charge in the area.

I can already predict their response — they usually give the same copy-paste reply to every genuine review. But I’m writing this so that others don’t fall into the same trap.

I sincerely hope authorities take note of such unethical practices, review their license, and take strict action.

I had heard good things about this doctor before, so I trusted her. But my delivery experience at Agrawal Hospital was honestly very bad and disappointing.

Throughout my pregnancy, I wasn’t prescribed any iron or multivitamin tablets. just calcium. When I asked for protein powder, they gave me one, but it didn’t help much. I also had other health issues like UTIs, but they were ignored completely.

On 21st May 2024, during my check-up, I told the doctor that I felt like my water was leaking, and that the flow seemed more than normal. But she didn’t ask for any scan or sonography.

Then on the night of 23rd May, I could barely feel my baby move. I panicked and got a sonography done on 24th May on my own, without the doctor’s advice. The report showed my amniotic fluid was low just 8%, which should ideally be at least 11%. Within 2 hours, I repeated the scan at another diagnostic center, and it had dropped to 7%.

I rushed back to show both reports to the doctor. But she said, “Don’t worry. Just eat vitamin C fruits and drink water. Come for your next check-up on 6th June.” My due date was 13th June.

The moment I reached home, my clothes were wet again. That’s when my husband rushed me to the hospital and told the doctor firmly: “If anything happens to the baby or mother, we will not sit quietly." Only then she asked for another scan. That scan showed my fluid was now 5.5%, my baby had very little movement and was in an uncomfortable, curled-up position.

Finally, at around 4:30 PM, she did the surgery.

The hospital bill was around ₹1.40 lakhs, plus ₹15,000 extra for all medicines and operation-related items that we had to buy ourselves. Nothing was provided by the hospital.

My daughter was born almost lifeless, struggling to breathe. And here’s the worst part — the hospital had no NICU, no baby care, and not even an ambulance. We had to shift her urgently to Sanjeevni Hospital, where she stayed in NICU for 2 days at ₹12,000 per day. We weren’t allowed to even see her properly. Every time my husband went to check on our baby, they charged ₹1,500 just to answer questions.

In total, we ended up spending ₹1.90 lakhs for a delivery that was poorly handled from the start.

Also, Agrawal Hospital doesn’t provide food, water, tea, breakfast, hospital gowns, or even a baby swaddle. Before admitting, if you ask, the reception will say “yes” to everything. But once you’re in, you’re on your own. You have to arrange everything yourself.

This is not how a hospital should treat expecting mothers. You don’t expect luxury, but at the very least, you expect care, responsibility, and basic facilities — especially when it’s a matter of life and death.

If you have 2L to spend I would suggest going to a better doctor and not her. She only performs C-section now. No Normal delivery. Plus, she is a careless female. If you love your life and your kids life... Avoid visiting her.

✈️ Ear Pain During Flight Travel

A Holiday Season Guide to Protect Your Ears 👂✨


---

🛫 Why Your Ears Hurt During Flights

During take-off and landing, cabin pressure changes rapidly. If your Eustachian tube doesn’t open properly, pressure builds behind the eardrum causing:
• Sharp ear pain
• Popping sounds
• Temporary hearing drop
• Fullness or pressure in the ear
• Ringing sensations

This is more common in winter because mild congestion, dryness, and allergies narrow the tube.


---

🔍 Who Is Most Sensitive?

• Children (small, narrow ear passages)
• Frequent flyers
• People recovering from a cold
• Sinusitis or allergic rhinitis patients
• Individuals with wax build-up


---

💡 Smart Tips for a Pain-Free Flight

🫗 Stay Hydrated
Sip water often — swallowing helps equalize ear pressure.

🍬 Chew or Suck
Use gum, lozenges, or frequent swallowing during take-off & landing.

👃 Nasal Preparation
Use a saline mist 30 minutes before boarding to keep passages open.

🧒 For Kids
Offer a bottle, snack, or pacifier during ascent & descent.

🛟 Special Technique: Valsalva Maneuver
Gently blow with nose pinched to pop ears safely — simple but effective.

🚫 Avoid Flying If
You have severe cold, ear infection, or intense sinus pressure.


---

Early ENT guidance ensures safer travel and prevents complications like middle-ear effusion, barotrauma, and prolonged hearing muffling.

🔊 Noise-Induced Hearing Loss (NIHL) – A Growing Modern-Day Concern!

👂 Noise-Induced Hearing Loss (NIHL) is one of the most preventable yet commonly overlooked causes of permanent hearing loss today. Prolonged or repeated exposure to loud sounds — from traffic, factories, concerts, earphones 🎧, or even daily gadgets — can damage delicate hair cells inside the inner ear. Once damaged, these cells do not regenerate, leading to permanent hearing impairment.

🚨 Common Warning Signs:

Ringing or buzzing in the ears (Tinnitus) 🎶

Difficulty hearing in crowded places 🗣️

Needing to increase TV or phone volume 📱

Ear discomfort or muffled hearing after loud events

🎧 At-Risk Groups:

People frequently using earphones or headphones at high volumes

Musicians, DJs, factory & construction workers 👷‍♂️

Urban dwellers exposed to constant traffic or machinery noise

🛡️ Prevention is Key:

Follow the 60/60 rule – keep volume below 60% for not more than 60 minutes at a stretch

Use noise-cancelling headphones

Wear ear protection in noisy environments

Schedule regular hearing check-ups with your ENT specialist 👨‍⚕️

✨ Remember: Once hearing loss occurs, it’s irreversible — but early detection and protection can preserve your hearing for life!
